introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0585 RELIGIOUS STUDIES 1, JUNE 2022, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the booklet is headed ORDINARY LEVEL - 0585 RELIGIOUS STUDIES 1. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question; if you change your mind, erase the first mark carefully, then mark your new answer. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet using the blank spaces. At the end of the examination the invigilator collects the answer sheet first and then the question booklet. The questions cover personal and social relationships and problems (sexuality, marriage and family, justice and peace, conscience, work, drugs, corruption, HIV/AIDS and related topics).

questions.enonce_markdown: Sexual abuse of a child by an adult is ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Paedophilia is the sexual abuse of, or sexual attraction to, a child by an adult. Rape is forced intercourse in general, abduction is taking a person away by force or deceit, and masochism is deriving pleasure from one's own pain.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: Peace is not only the absence of war but the presence of ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the usual teaching, peace is more than the absence of war: it is the fruit of justice, where each person receives what is due to them. Transparency and accountability are qualities of good governance, and love is a motive for peace rather than its defining condition here.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - peace and reconciliation
O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: This type of love is intense, full of excitement and does not last long.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Infatuation is a passionate but short-lived attraction. Agape is selfless, lasting love, conjugal love is the love between spouses, and filial love is the love between parents and children.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these is not related to sects and cults?

*Options as printed:* A) Their leaders do not manipulate them.   B) Both do not deal with secrecy.   C) It promotes promiscuity.   D) Sects are religious while cults are demonic.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sects and cults are usually described as groups that are secretive and whose leaders control their members, so the statement 'Their leaders do not manipulate them' is the one that is not related to them. The other statements are also debatable (for example, that sects are religious and cults demonic).

**Intended answer: A (Their leaders do not manipulate them).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults

questions.enonce_markdown: Family which is made up of father, mother and children is known as ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A nuclear family consists of a father, a mother and their children. An extended family also includes other relatives such as grandparents, uncles and aunts.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Surrogacy is ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the usual teaching, surrogacy is an arrangement in which a woman carries a pregnancy for another person or couple, commonly called womb hiring. Egg donation, artificial insemination and embryo transfer are techniques that may be used but are not the name of the arrangement.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following can best guarantee justice in a society?

*Options as printed:* A) Fear of laws   B) The lawyers   C) The Magistrates   D) The fear of God
questions.corrige_markdown:
Many programmes answer that the fear of God best guarantees justice, because it acts on the conscience even where no one is watching, while laws, lawyers and magistrates only work where they can see and enforce. Answers differ with the textbook and the tradition.

**Intended answer: D (The fear of God).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: Sexual intercourse between close family members is called ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Incest is sexual relations between close relatives. Fornication is between unmarried people, adultery involves a married person with someone who is not their spouse, and rape is forced intercourse.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: We should respect our bodies because we...
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Christian teaching, the human body deserves respect because the person is created by God. Obeying the law, equal dignity and the risk of diseases do not give the basic reason asked for.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity
O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown:
A person who has no home and wanders about is called a/an...

*Options as printed:* A) traveller.   B) (option B cut off in the scan)   C) vagus.   D) incola.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A person with no fixed home who wanders about is called a vagus in moral and marriage law (compare question 35). An incola, on the contrary, has a domicile. Option B is cut off in the scan.

**Intended answer: C (vagus).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - homelessness and vagrancy

questions.enonce_markdown: The main purpose of a trade union is to...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A trade union is formed to defend and improve the working conditions and interests of workers (pay, hours, safety). Output and quality are the employer's concern, and preventing every dismissal is not its aim.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and unemployment

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is a primary source of global warming?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Global warming is mainly caused by greenhouse gases, above all carbon dioxide released by burning fuels and by industry. Ozone depletion is a different problem, and the sun's rays are natural.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - environmental ethics

questions.enonce_markdown: When one parent is forced by circumstances to bring up children alone, he/she is known as a...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The term that covers either a father or a mother raising children alone, as the question says he/she, is single parent. Single mother and widow apply to women only, and separated parent describes only one cause.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: A drug that can lead to a prolonged mental disorder when abused is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Marijuana (cannabis) is the substance the programme links to lasting mental disorder when abused. Gin, alcohol and whisky are alcoholic drinks, whose main effects stressed in the programme are addiction and damage to the liver.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - drugs and substance abuse

questions.enonce_markdown: Sexual relations between two females.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Lesbianism is the term for sexual relations between two women. Homosexuality is the wider term for same-sex attraction or relations between either sex, masturbation is self-stimulation, and sexual intercourse does not specify the partners.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown:
The transfer of public funds into private accounts abroad is known as ...

*Options as printed:* A) money laundry.   B) capital flight.   C) money transfer.   D) embezzlement.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sending public funds into private accounts abroad is capital flight (money leaving the country illegally). Embezzlement is the dishonest use of funds entrusted to one's care and is also defensible.

**Intended answer: B (capital flight).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown: The abbreviation HIV stands for...
questions.corrige_markdown:
HIV stands for Human Immunodeficiency Virus: a virus that attacks the body's immune system. Option A is the printed form closest to this (with the spelling error 'Immuned'); the others drop the word 'Deficiency'.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - hiv and aids

questions.enonce_markdown: It is a requirement of an ordinary Christian marriage.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A valid Christian wedding requires the spouses, the witnesses and the minister who receives their consent. Parents and the congregation are welcome but not required for validity.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

choix.texte: The couples must be present in church.
The minister, parents and Christians must be in church.
The couples, witnesses and the minister must be in church.
The official, parents and Christians must be in church.

questions.enonce_markdown: The practice of running away with a young woman and making her a wife without a traditional pre-authorization and recognition is called ....
questions.corrige_markdown:
Taking a young woman away to make her a wife without the consent and recognition of her family is abduction. Polyandry is one woman with several husbands, seduction is enticing someone, and cohabitation is living together without being married.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is it wrong for believers in God to consult a soothsayer?
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to Christian teaching, consulting soothsayers and diviners is forbidden by the commandments of God, because it puts trust in them instead of God. The other options are judgements about the persons, not the reason given by the teaching.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

choix.texte: They are agents of the devil.
Their actions are forbidden by the commandments of God.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the human faculty responsible for determining the morality of the human action?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The conscience is the inner faculty by which a person judges whether an act is right or wrong. The mind, the brain and the soul are broader and are not specifically the moral judge.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown:
Estella decides to cut off her hand because she wants to get rid of her cancer infected finger. Such a phenomenon is known as ...........

*Options as printed:* A) principle of mutilation.   B) principle of cloning.   C) Principle of double effect.   D) Principle of equity.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sacrificing a diseased part of the body to save the whole person is justified by the principle of totality, which is not among the options. Of the printed options, mutilation is the closest name for the act of cutting off the hand.

**Intended answer: A (principle of mutilation).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown: When a brother by law marries the wife of his late brother who dies childless, this marriage type is referred to as ................
questions.corrige_markdown:
Levirate marriage is the custom by which a man marries the widow of his deceased brother, especially to raise children for him. Sororate marriage is the reverse: a man marries his late wife's sister.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: The love of God for making can best be termed...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The love of God for humankind is the selfless, unconditional love called agape. Storge is family affection, philia is friendship and eros is passionate love. The stem is printed 'for making' (probably 'mankind').

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown: Erotic love centres on......
questions.corrige_markdown:
Erotic love (eros) centres on sexual desire and attraction, here expressed as genital sex and exchange of gifts. Self-giving is the mark of agape.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

choix.texte: genital sex and exchange of gifts.
self-giving, exchange of gifts and giving praises.
enjoying yourself and exchange of gifts.

questions.enonce_markdown:
This best describes love ...

*Options as printed:* A) Not wicked and jealous.   B) Boastful and selfish.   C) Takes little pleasure over other people's sin.   D) (option D cut off in the scan)
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the well-known description of love, love does not rejoice at wrongdoing, so 'takes little pleasure over other people's sin' fits best. Option A is garbled and D is cut off in the scan.

**Intended answer: C (Takes little pleasure over other people's sin).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - friendship and love

questions.enonce_markdown: Another name for marriage is .........
questions.corrige_markdown:
Matrimony is a synonym of marriage. Monogamy is a type of marriage (one spouse), while model and maturity are unrelated.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: Justin had sex with Mary against her will, Justin is charged for:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sexual intercourse against a person's will is rape. Adultery and fornication concern consensual relations.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity
O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown:
To say that marriage is enduring and exclusive means .............

*Options as printed:* A) it is a covenant between God and humans.   B) it is a covenant between man and woman.   C) it must be forever between man and woman.   D) it must be forever till death do them part.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Marriage is called enduring because it lasts until death, and exclusive because it is between one man and one woman. Option D expresses the lasting side, while C expresses the exclusive side; both are defensible.

**Intended answer: D (it must be forever till death do them part).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: A validly married man cannot divorce his wife to marry another woman because of the impediment of .........
questions.corrige_markdown:
The impediment of previous bond means that a person already validly married cannot marry another while the first spouse lives. Consanguinity is blood relationship and affinity is relationship by marriage.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: If a married man hires killers to eliminate his wife for him to marry another woman, it is invalid because of the impediment of ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The impediment of crime applies when someone causes the death of a spouse in order to marry another person, so that marriage is invalid. Abduction, consanguinity and affinity describe other situations.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - marriage and family

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following is not a reason for fornication:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Peer pressure, curiosity and economic hardship are commonly given reasons why unmarried people have sexual relations. Infidelity of a partner presupposes a committed, usually married, relationship and is not a reason for fornication as such, so it is the odd one out.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown: What is bestiality?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Bestiality is sexual relations between a human being and an animal.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

choix.texte: Sexual relation between a person and an animal.
Sexual relations between beasts of different species.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The best peace one can aspire for is...

*Options as printed:* A) domestic peace.   B) celestial peace.   C) environmental peace.   D) social peace.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Many textbooks give celestial (heavenly) peace as the highest peace to aim for, but this depends on a religious belief.

**Intended answer: B (celestial peace).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - peace and reconciliation

questions.enonce_markdown: This best describes a vagus.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the Church's marriage law, a vagus is a person who has no domicile or quasi-domicile anywhere, that is, no fixed place of residence. An incola has a domicile, so the permanent or temporary home options do not describe a vagus.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - homelessness and vagrancy

choix.texte: One who is in a place of permanent home.
One who is in a place of temporal home.
One who is out of his home and still retains his home.
One who has no where to lay his/her head.

questions.enonce_markdown: A method of artificial birth control is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
An implant is an artificial (device or hormone based) contraceptive. Coitus interruptus, cervical mucus and the calendar are classed as natural methods.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics
O Level Religious Studies - sexuality and chastity

questions.enonce_markdown:
Why do people work?

*Options as printed:* A) To have a high living Standard.   B) To be richer.   C) To be fruitful and multiply.   D) To produce necessary goods and services.
questions.corrige_markdown:
People work mainly to produce the goods and services that society needs and to earn a living. A high living standard is also a defensible answer.

**Intended answer: D (To produce necessary goods and services).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and unemployment

questions.enonce_markdown: An organization aimed at promoting the rights and interest of its workers is known as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A trade union is the organization formed to promote and protect the rights and interests of workers. An employers' association defends employers instead, and the last option is not a standard term.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - work and unemployment

questions.enonce_markdown: Mr. Mark disconnected the drips his brother has been receiving in the hospital so he could die and rest from the pain of blood cancer, what name can we give to Mr. Mark's action?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Ending a suffering person's life to relieve pain is called euthanasia (mercy killing). It is not suicide, because it is another person's life that is ended, and not mutilation, which is harming a body part.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following best describes suicide?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Suicide is the deliberate taking of one's own life. Taking another person's life is killing or murder.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sanctity of life and bioethics

choix.texte: To take away another person's life.

questions.enonce_markdown:
One of the causes of drug abuse is ...

*Options as printed:* A) lack of employment.   B) poor preservation.   C) lack of education.   D) economic brain drains.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Lack of employment is a commonly given cause of drug abuse among the youth, but lack of education is also defensible.

**Intended answer: A (lack of employment).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: O Level Religious Studies - drugs and substance abuse

questions.enonce_markdown: The inner voice which helps us in judging whether something is right or wrong is known as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The conscience is the inner voice that tells a person whether an act is right or wrong.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown: When the intellect judges an act only after it has been done, it is known as...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In moral teaching, a consequent conscience judges an act after it has been done, an antecedent conscience judges before, and a concomitant conscience judges during the act. A perplexed conscience is one torn between two apparent duties.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown: The conscience that helps the possessor to be honest at all the times is called...
questions.corrige_markdown:
A sincere conscience is an honest one that seeks the truth and acts on it. A perplexed conscience cannot decide and a lax conscience excuses wrongdoing too easily. A certain conscience is firm about a judgement but is not specifically about honesty.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - conscience and moral choice

questions.enonce_markdown: For peace to reign in a society, there must be...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Peace in a society rests on justice, where rights are respected and each person receives what is due. This agrees with the usual teaching that peace is the fruit of justice.

**Answer: D.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - peace and reconciliation
O Level Religious Studies - justice and human rights

questions.enonce_markdown: These ills rank first in the Cameroon society:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the programme's treatment of social ills in Cameroon, bribery and corruption are given as the leading ones. The other pairs are real problems but are not ranked first there.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown: Giving undue favour to a person only because you are relatives is known as ...
questions.corrige_markdown:
Nepotism is favouring relatives, for example in jobs, because of the family tie. Favouritism is the general term, and tribalism is favouring people of one's tribe.

**Answer: C.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - corruption and embezzlement

questions.enonce_markdown: The most dangerous tree to the water table is...
questions.corrige_markdown:
The eucalyptus is a fast-growing tree with very high water use, so it can lower the water table. Fig, guava and baobab trees are not known for this.

**Answer: B.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - environmental ethics

questions.enonce_markdown: Dealing with evil spirits intended to harm and cause suffering is called...
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the usual classification, diabolic witchcraft is dealing with evil spirits to harm others and cause suffering. The other options refer to different kinds of so-called witchcraft.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - sects and cults

questions.enonce_markdown: This is the most common problem that Information and Communication Technology (ICT) has brought to Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The most common problem linked to ICT in the programme is cyber criminality (internet fraud and related offences). Poor network is a technical shortcoming and the other options are not a main problem.

**Answer: A.**
themes: O Level Religious Studies - ict and society
